svg.title: Volume versus temperature for a real gas
svg.desc: Volume versus temperature at constant pressure. Above about −183 °C the gas follows the ideal-gas straight line, which extrapolates (dashed) to zero volume at −273.15 °C. At about −183 °C the gas condenses to a liquid and the volume drops almost to zero; at about −218 °C the liquid freezes to a solid, a further small decrease. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.
